specialRules.ruleFull: Wood elves move through forest and woodland terrain with no penalty.
A wood elf spots a hidden enemy from twice as far away as other warriors, so twice his Initiative in inches.
A wood elf will never use a blackpowder weapon, and will never wear heavy armour of any kind except ithilmar.
The warband will never hire a hired sword or dramatis persona who is not an elf.

The first time any wood elf henchman rolls That Lad's Got Talent, re-roll the dice and take the second result, even if it is That Lad's Got Talent again. Any later result of That Lad's Got Talent counts as normal; only the first rolled for each henchmen group is re-rolled.
Any warrior within 6" of the Way-Warden may use his Leadership for a Leadership test.
The Spellweaver casts from the Fey Magic list. He may cast no spell while he wears armour.
While the warband holds a Wild Hunter it may buy 0-3 of each beast companion its lists allow. A beast bought this way may use the Wild Hunter's Leadership for a test while it is within 6" of him.

fighters.name: Pathfinder
fighters.equipment: A Pathfinder must always carry a missile weapon.

specialRules.ruleFull: While a Pathfinder is hiding, enemy models suffer -1 to their Initiative for working out whether they detect him.
A Wardancer may use neither a missile weapon nor armour.
A Wardancer has a 6+ armour save that is never modified, and ignores a spell that targets or affects him on a D6 roll of 6.
A Wardancer may always try to parry, whatever weapon he uses. Fighting with a sword he may re-roll a failed parry, as though he carried a buckler and a sword; two swords give him nothing more.
A Wolfhound is an animal and gains no experience.
A Wolfhound may only be included while the warband holds a Wild Hunter.
While one or more wolves are in base contact with the same opponent as the Wild Hunter, a Wolfhound gains +1 to hit that opponent. The bonus does not stack when more than one wolf is in base contact.
A Hunting Cat is an animal and gains no experience.
A Hunting Cat may only be included while the warband holds a Wild Hunter.
If a Hunting Cat charges an opponent and hits with both attacks, whether or not it wounds, the target must pass a Strength test or be knocked down. It has no effect on a large target.
The model causes fear.
A Wood Spirit has a 4+ armour save.
Not affected by any poison.
A Wood Spirit takes double wounds from a fire attack.
The model is immune to psychology and never leaves combat.
A Wood Spirit gains experience at half rate and may never become a hero.

skillGroup.name: Animal Aspects
skillGroup.note: Wood Elf heroes only. No more than two heroes in a warband may hold the same Aspect.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Hawk
specialSkillsList.description: Only a model with Quickshot may take this. He may shoot twice a turn with a bow, long bow, elf bow or gladewood bow and ignores the to-hit penalty for moving, though the normal limits on moving more than his base move still hold. It may not be combined with Quickshot to make more than two shots a turn.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Serpent
specialSkillsList.description: If the model does not move, it scores a critical hit with a missile weapon against a target within short range on a roll of 5 or 6.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Panther
specialSkillsList.description: While hidden, the warrior may shoot a missile weapon and stay hidden. If the target is neither stunned nor taken out of action by the attack it may take an Initiative test; if it passes, it sees the attacker, who is no longer hidden.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Fox
specialSkillsList.description: The warrior is always placed on the battlefield after the opposing warband, anywhere on the table that is out of sight of it and more than 12" from any enemy model. If both players have models with this skill or with Infiltration, roll a D6 for each and the lowest sets up first.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Stag
specialSkillsList.description: Only one hero in a warband may take this, and a Spellweaver may not. He may now choose skills from the Strength list.

specialSkillsList.name: Aspect of the Rabbit
specialSkillsList.description: The warrior avoids a melee or missile attack on a roll of 6. If he also has Step Aside or Dodge, that becomes a 4+ in the matching area.

rules.text: With this weapon a roll of 2-4 counts as Stunned when rolling for the extent of a model's injuries.

A wood elf with the Asrai Bladestaff may parry as a sword does. When his opponent rolls to hit, he may roll a D6; if it beats the opponent's highest roll to hit, the blow is parried and that attack is discarded. No attack made with double his own Strength or more may be parried.

rules.name: Additional attack
rules.text: The user gains an extra attack with this weapon, and the normal rules for fighting with two weapons then apply.

rules.name: Power shot
rules.text: If the wielder does not move in his movement phase, every shot at a target within short range, 15", counts as Strength 4.

rules.name: Deerhide
rules.text: Deerhide leather armour works exactly as light armour, giving a 6+ armour save, but may not be combined with any other armour except a helmet or a buckler. It may not be sold back at the trading post.

rules.name: Birch Wine
rules.text: A warband that drinks birch wine before a battle is immune to fear and to Stunned results for the whole of that battle. One use only.

rules.name: Enchanted Acorns
rules.text: Roll D3+1 for how many acorns are acquired. When a hero has to roll on the Serious Injury chart and the result is 11-35, he may consume one acorn, and only one, to re-roll the first die; so on a 14, with at least one acorn, the 1 may be re-rolled. The second result must be accepted and may not be re-rolled. Note the acorn used and remove it from his equipment.

rules.name: Blood Ivy
rules.text: A model wounded by an arrow of blood ivy must pass a Toughness test at once or suffer -1 Strength for the rest of the battle. The effects of several such arrows do not stack. There are enough arrows to last one campaign.

rules.name: Falcon
rules.text: A falcon lets you change one die roll in the exploration phase by 1, up or down, as long as its owning hero was not taken out of action in the battle. Only one falcon per warband.

rules.name: Forest Familiar
rules.text: A forest familiar gives the Wild Hunter +2" on his spotting distance for detecting hidden enemies. Once per game its presence may also allow any model within 6" of the Wild Hunter to re-roll a roll; that re-roll may not itself be re-rolled.

flags.what: The PDF's text layer is broken into single letters and holds none of the profiles or the skill table, so pages 2, 6 and 7 were opened as images to read them.
An Asrai Way-farers warband needs at least three models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported.

The skill table: Way-Warden Combat, Shooting, Academic, Speed, Special; Spellweaver Shooting, Academic, Speed, Special; Wild Hunter Combat, Strength, Speed, Special; Pathfinder Combat, Shooting, Speed, Special.
No maximum profile is printed, so every elf takes our Elf maximum.
The Aspect of the Stag is headed "(0-1)", so only one hero may take it; the group's own limit of two heroes per Aspect is its note.

The starred list prices are "the cost of equipment purchased by starting warbands before leaving their homelands", which is what a list price already is, so no rule is imported for it. The item entries' own prices and rarities are what the store uses.
The Ithilmar Weapon line is "3x weapon cost", which is kept as the line's note; ours already carries the same. Ithilmar Armour is 80 gc here against our 90: only the starting list price is theirs.
The Elven Cloak (80+2D6, Rare 10), the Healing Herbs (20+2D6, Rare 7) and the Hunting Arrows (35 gc, common) are ours with a price row each; ours are 100 gc Rare 12, 20 gc Rare 8 and 25 gc Rare 8.
The Forest Familiar (+2" spotting for the Wild Hunter) is not our Familiar and is kept apart; the Enchanted Acorns are not the Marienburg Magic Acorn. See the decisions.
The Spellweaver's rules call him a "Spellwalker", as does the Aspect of the Stag; he is the Spellweaver throughout.
The Wood Spirit gains experience at half rate and may never become a hero; our templates hold no half rate, so he gains experience and is not promotable, and the rule says the rest.
The Fey Magic list is imported as the lore Fey Magic: Angering Spites 7, Oakskin 7, Terrifying Spites 8, Fury of the Wild 8, Ever-Living Resplendence 6, Call of the Hunt 9.
No group sizes are printed for the henchmen.
